FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.96
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not sandbox tests against the patched source tree; it only writes the single patched file into a temp directory, then runs `test_cmd` with `cwd=tmpdir`. The provided integration path from `immune_agents.py` calls `evaluate_fixes(..., test_cmd=["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...])`. In that sandbox, `bench/tests/` does not exist, and even if tests are discovered via an absolute/import path, imports resolve against the real project tree because only one file was copied. Evidence in `bench/endocrine.py`: `patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))` and no project tree copy; tests are run unchanged with `_run_tool(test_cmd, cwd=tmpdir)`. This violates the module’s own contract: “sandboxed (tempdir, never modifies actual source)” and prevents meaningful end-to-end fix evaluation.
FOLLOW: Downstream, the “Fix evaluation” feature does not actually test the proposed fix in isolation against the project. That causes two bad outcomes: (1) false HARMFUL/UNEVALUABLE verdicts when pytest cannot find `bench/tests/` from the temp dir, so valid fixes are not marked verified; (2) false SAFE/NEUTRAL verdicts when tests or imports execute against the real source tree instead of the patched file, so the endocrine layer can certify a fix that was never exercised. This crosses the interface into `immune_agents.py` Stage 4, where SAFE/NEUTRAL results set `finding.verified = True`; if the sandbox is testing the wrong tree, the bug-closed gate can close findings on invalid evidence, silently corrupting reviewer-facing state.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — sandbox a minimal project tree, not a single file: create `tmpdir/bench`, copy the relevant source tree (at least all `source_paths` plus `bench/tests` if present), apply the patch to the copied target file at its relative path, and run `test_cmd` against that copied tree. Keep `cwd=tmpdir` so tests and imports resolve only within the sandbox.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.89
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.47
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` can mark a fix SAFE even when it introduces new issues, because it sums net deltas across different tools and only checks `total_net > 0`. Example: `net_type_errors = +5`, `net_ruff_errors = -6`, `net_bandit_issues = 0` yields `total_net = -1`, so verdict becomes SAFE despite five new type errors. Evidence in `bench/endocrine.py`: `total_net = result.net_type_errors + result.net_ruff_errors + result.net_bandit_issues`; `if total_net > 0: HARMFUL`, `if total_net < 0: SAFE`. The function’s own docstring says “HARMFUL: new issues introduced”, which this logic violates.
FOLLOW: Downstream, the endocrine layer can certify regressions as SAFE whenever one checker’s improvement numerically offsets another checker’s breakage. That directly undermines Stage 4 in `immune_agents.py`, where SAFE/NEUTRAL marks a finding verified. A fix that adds fresh pyright or bandit failures can therefore become `verified=True`, feeding the NK bug-closed gate and causing later duplicate findings to be auto-closed on a broken fix. This is a silently wrong-result path, not just a scoring quirk.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — treat any positive per-tool delta as HARMFUL before computing overall improvement: if `result.net_type_errors > 0 or result.net_ruff_errors > 0 or result.net_bandit_issues > 0`, return `"HARMFUL"`. Only return SAFE when no per-tool delta is positive and at least one is negative, or tests pass with all deltas zero.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.83
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.52
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` measures pre-fix diagnostics on the original file path but post-fix diagnostics on a standalone temp file with a different location and no surrounding project/config context. Static analyzers such as pyright, ruff, and bandit can change behavior based on repository root, config discovery, imports, excludes, and neighboring modules. Evidence: pre counts use `_count_tool_issues(..., target_path)`; post counts use `_count_tool_issues(..., patched_path)` where `patched_path` is just `tmpdir/basename.py`. This is not a like-for-like comparison.
FOLLOW: Downstream, net deltas can be dominated by environment drift rather than the patch itself. A fix may appear to improve because the temp file no longer sees project-level config or import graph, or appear to worsen because path-based settings differ. That contaminates SAFE/HARMFUL/NEUTRAL outputs and therefore the `verified` flag propagation in `immune_agents.py`. The feature fires, but its verdicts are mechanically unsound and can mislead the reviewer.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — compare before and after in the same sandboxed project context: copy the relevant tree into tempdir, run pre-fix tool counts on the copied unmodified target there, apply the patch in place, then run post-fix counts on the same copied path.
VERIFIED: TRUE

This makes the health report claim the tool ran successfully when no scan occurred.
